questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The history of women getting the vote in Britain
How general elections work in the UK and Europe
Efforts to get more women to stand for parliament
Why politics on TV is so boring for young people
questions.why: They discuss projects trying to get more women interested in standing for parliament.

questions.q: What does Georgina say about women MPs in the UK?
options: About 34% are women, the most ever but far from half
Half of all MPs are now women, for the first time
The number of women MPs has been falling for years
There are no women MPs under the age of 30
questions.why: She says about 34% of MPs are women, the highest ever, but still not close to 50%.

options: Asking more young people to vote in elections
Raising money for women's charities across the UK
Training young journalists to report on politics
Getting more women interested in standing as MPs
questions.why: Sam describes it as one of the projects trying to get more women interested in standing for parliament.

questions.q: How did Lucrece Grehoua feel about politics at first?
options: She had wanted to be a politician since childhood
She thought it looked boring and not for her
She was angry at all politicians for lying
She found it much too difficult to follow
questions.why: She says she didn't see herself in Parliament and politics looked extremely boring.

questions.q: What made Lucrece decide to sign up?
options: A well-known politician asked her to join
Her family and friends encouraged her to try
It included a diverse range of young women
She was offered a paid job in parliament
questions.why: She says when she saw it included a diverse range of young women, she thought 'this is really for me'.

questions.q: What does Lucrece believe about everybody and politics?
options: Only well-educated people can understand politics
We all get angry about something, so we're all politicians
Most people don't really care about politics at all
Young people should stay out of politics until they're older
questions.why: She says, “everybody has a politician within them because we all get anger about something.”

questions.q: What did Lucrece dislike about the way politics is discussed?
options: It is too emotional and people shout too much
It happens only on TV late at night
It is always about money and taxes
It is full of jargon that's hard to understand
questions.why: She says when we see it, it's all jargon, not words we can understand.

questions.q: Why does Lucrece mention her working-class, disadvantaged background?
options: To show politics is for everyone if explained well
To explain why she can't stand for parliament yet
To complain about private schools and their pupils
To ask the listeners for some financial help
questions.why: She says she realised politics is for everybody; the way you speak about it has to be tailored to everyone.
